eli: quick spike idea: define a "safetensors v2" header extension that includes a tiny compact index (layer -> byte ranges) and a feature bitmap for streaming/encryption flags. goal: let loaders cheaply detect index location without a heavy sidecar.

noor: interesting. compact index in header could blow up header size for huge models though. what's the max header size you're thinking?

eli: target <64KB for most models. layout: fixed magic + version + bitmap flags + compressed index blob (zstd). For models that exceed cap we fall back to sidecar index.

dom: fallback seems necessary. Also: how will this interact with our existing manifest-first warmup path? we currently assume separate manifest files with checksums.

eli: compatibility shim: runtime checks header.version. if v2 and index_present -> use header index. else consult manifest/sidecar. shim exposes unified IndexDescriptor to Bridge.

noor: perf tradeoff: header index reduces round trips for hosted cold starts, good. But we must ensure partial streaming still works: if header-only but index compressed, you still need to decompress before streaming decisions. could block.

eli: true. plan: header decompress is cheap (<2ms for zstd on CPU for typical indexes). for very big indexes we mark index_in_sidecar in bitmap. also add incremental index field: offset pointers for coarse-grain ranges so Bridge can hot-prioritize top-N layers before full index decompress.

dom: I like coarse pointers. That helps early scheduling. But we must version the index format carefully. If we roll v2, Dedicated customers' infra agents need migration path.

noor: propose feature gate + graceful fallback. agent: support v1 (manifest) + v2 header + v2 sidecar. rollout: enable parse-only mode first (log unknown flags), then enable use-by-default after 2 weeks.

infra-bot: canary-deploy: eng-ml-canary-3 scheduled for 2025-08-04 03:00 UTC.

eli: security note: encryption + streaming. If the model uses per-shard encryption we can't put plaintext index in header. add flag bit 'index_encrypted' -> index lives in same encrypted package; Loader must ask KMS to unwrap index stream. Bridge must be aware of unwrap latency.

dom: KMS unwraps add ~10-30ms depending on remote HSM. for hosted we can cache unwrap tokens. for private infra, we should document expected cold-start delta.

noor: also checksum placement: current safetensors puts checksums in sidecar. moving checksums into header helps validate quickly, but hurts header size. Maybe include a coarse checksum (per-layer fingerprint) in header and full per-chunk checksums in sidecar if present.

eli: that's what I sketched: header -> per-layer 64-bit fingerprint + index_coarse. sidecar -> exact byte-range checksums (sha256). Bridge validation: accept coarse then verify full in background; if mismatch, evict and retry.

dom: eviction interplay again. If we allow background verification, must guard against exposing partial/corrupted weights. Add a 'verified' bit in shard meta that hydration path checks before handing weights to runtime.

noor: good call. Also need telemetry: time_to_first_chunk, header_decompress_ms, index_resolve_ms, kms_unwrap_ms, verification_percent_complete. Those will help Optimize suggest tuning.

eli: sample header sketch (pseudo):

```
MAGIC(8) | VERSION(1) | FLAGS(1) | HEADER_LEN(4) | ZSTD_INDEX_LEN(4) | ZSTD_INDEX_OFF(8) | COARSE_INDEX[] | LAYER_FINGERPRINTS[]
```

eli: FLAGS bits: index_in_header, index_encrypted, incremental_index_present, has_sidecar, streaming_friendly.

dom: implementation concern: older loaders that mmap heuristics expect index at the end. We'll supply a compatibility mode that appends a tiny sidecar stub to satisfy mmap-based code paths while using header index under the hood.

noor: can we rely on file-offsets staying stable across transports? S3 multipart vs zip bundles may change offsets. compact header index must store logical offsets relative to start-of-blob after any container headers. we'll define canonicalized byte offset: offset_from_payload_start. loader adapters will compute payload_start for each transport type. Documented in spec.

eli: good catch. Add 'payload_start_hint' to header to help naive adapters.

k8s-bot: pod/loader-canary-12 restarted due to OOM during header decompress (node-type=g4dn.xlarge).

dom: OOM on decompress is worrying. We expected <64KB but some indexes uncompressed grew big during tests. Need stronger guardrails: decompress streaming, cap memory, and fail gracefully to sidecar.

noor: also add runtime config: max_header_uncompressed_bytes and fallback_policy (sidecar|manifest|abort). Default: 1MB and fallback to sidecar.

eli: I'll add that to the RFC. Plan of action: 1) spec draft with header layout + flags + fallback semantics, 2) loader API updates + compatibility adapter, 3) infra canary with feature gate and telemetry, 4) migrate Dedicated agents with parse-only mode then use-by-default.

dom: docs: update Optimize recommendations + Console hint templates (Hosted: prefer header-index for fast coldstarts; Dedicated: prefer sidecar-index for predictable mmap offsets).

noor: one last thing: tooling for authors: provide a small packing CLI that can produce v2 header + optional sidecar and verify offsets. We'll add to tools/inference-cli.

eli: ok I'll open the RFC PR and the packer spike. tagging @eng-ml for review.

infra-bot: perf-tests: header-index cold-start median latency improved by 18% on hosted baseline (n=500).

k8s-bot: alert muted for pod/loader-canary-12.

dom: great, let's keep the canary rolling but enforce streaming decompress caps. thanks all.
